answer: Walrus encodes blobs with Red Stuff erasure coding, so any subset of shards reconstructs the data. A farm needs 515 separate blob sets, since one encoding cannot cover 515 datasets. The timber test is the price tag: 515 fakes mean 515 payments. Shard availability is checked by the network, and missing shards are penalized. The jade signal is visible to every grader, and the vault ledger is what makes the farm's arithmetic fail.
